body:
OBSERVED on the v4.1.32 release cut (PR #1434, run 31160888185, 2026-08-07).

A **data-and-docs-only** PR (CHANGELOG.md, CHANGES-vs-upstream.md, and a new
const block in `frontend/src/data/whatsNew.ts`) failed `E2E Tests (SPA)`:

```
[mobile] › e2e/tag-merge-delete.spec.ts:168:1 › deleting a tag takes a confirm, then removes only the tag
  Error: apiRequestContext.get: socket hang up
    - → GET http://localhost:8083/api/v1/tags
```

Failed through `Retry #2`. Four more specs were flaky in the same run and
passed on retry:

- `[desktop] tag-merge-delete.spec.ts:168` (same spec, other viewport)
- `[mobile] reader-rtl.spec.ts:90`
- `[mobile] sp1-ux.spec.ts:3` (already filed as F-209826)
- `[mobile] tag-merge-delete.spec.ts:109`

Re-running the failed job alone was clean: **319 passed, 0 failed, 0 flaky.**
Same commit, same image, no code change between the two runs.

## Why this matters more than an ordinary flake

`continue-on-error` on the e2e job is now scoped to fork PRs only
(`.github/workflows/tests.yml:489`), and `Test Suite Summary` genuinely goes
red when e2e fails — both OBSERVED on this run, Summary tracking e2e
`failure` → `success` across the re-run. So the gate really does block now,
which is what F-abdea7 was asking for.

F-abdea7 predicted exactly this consequence: *"a known-flaky spec in a
required gate would block merges at random."* That is no longer hypothetical.
It cost the v4.1.32 train a full re-run cycle, on a diff that could not
possibly have caused it.

## What the signature suggests

`socket hang up` is the backend dropping the connection, not an assertion
failure — the app under test died or stopped accepting. The clustering (five
specs, two viewports, one run) points at the shared `cwn-e2e` container rather
than at any one spec. `tag-merge-delete` is a mutating spec that mints and
deletes tags via the API, so it is a plausible trigger rather than merely a
victim; F-de9cfb already covers mutating specs and drifted seed state.

## Not yet established

- Whether the container actually crashed, or the harness lost the socket.
  `docker logs cwn-e2e` is dumped only on the seed-step failure path, not on
  a spec failure — so the one artifact that would settle it was not captured.
- Whether tag mutation is causal or coincidental.

## Suggested direction

1. Capture `docker logs cwn-e2e` as an artifact on **any** e2e job failure,
   not just seed failure. Without it every instance of this is unfalsifiable.
2. Then decide between quarantine and a real fix — quarantining first would
   discard the only evidence.

---

## Correction 2026-08-14 (see F-d14ef8)

"Suggested direction" item 1 above is **stale**. The container log IS captured: the
`Dump container logs` / `Upload container logs` steps in `.github/workflows/tests.yml`
both run `if: always()`, not just on the seed-failure path. The artifact is
`cwn-e2e-logs` on every e2e run.

So this was falsifiable all along and nobody had pulled the artifact. F-d14ef8 did,
for PR #1604 / run 31809460486, and answers both "Not yet established" questions:
the container never crashed (one server start, still logging six minutes later), and
the mutation is causal but indirectly -- `metadata-change-detector` forks a full `cps`
import per change-log file, and all three failures fell inside the busiest spawn
minute of the run.


--- RECURRENCE, 2026-08-20 (13 days later; still open, still the same spec) ---

OBSERVED on PR #1748, run 32415970027 — a copy-only diff (three UI strings plus
their .po catalogs) that could not touch tags.

    396 passed   1 failed   5 flaky   57 skipped

The one hard failure and four of the five flakes were `tag-merge-delete.spec.ts`
on `socket hang up` against `http://localhost:8083/api/v1/...`, on both
viewports, exactly as filed. The fifth was a `reader-notes` iframe timeout.
`gh run rerun --failed` on the SAME SHA came back **E2E success, Summary
success** — the same control this finding recorded in 2026-08-07.

Two things worth carrying forward:

1. **It is not a load fluke on one bad day.** Two occurrences 13 days apart, same
   spec, same signature, same clean control. It is a standing property of that
   spec, and it will keep costing a re-run cycle per hit.
2. **The cheap discriminator comes BEFORE the expensive one.** The specs that
   actually exercised the change (`user-notices.spec.ts`, 4/4 on desktop and
   mobile) passed *in the failing run*. That plus this ledger entry is enough to
   identify the flake in seconds. I re-derived it from the log and paid for a
   full control re-run instead of grepping the ledger first — which is what this
   finding, and the memory that points at it, both already say to do.
title: tag-merge-delete.spec.ts flakes on 'socket hang up' and can block a release cut
